LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Melody. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can interesting melodies be created?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody
2. state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition
3. create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m
4. model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques
5. enjoy creating short melodies and modelling using clay. • roll clay into slab and cut out three rectangular pieces of three different sizes, • model so-lfa syllables (d r m) using coil technique and attach on the slabs

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: MELODY
This lesson teaches Melody for Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
3. create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
4. model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
5. enjoy creating short melodies and modelling using clay. • roll clay into slab and cut out three rectangular pieces of three different sizes, • model so-lfa syllables (d r m) using coil technique and attach on the slabs
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Melody using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Melody above.
2. Explain Melody to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Melody.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Melody with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Melody important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can interesting melodies be created?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody
2. state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition
3. create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m
4. model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
